name: unrelated-weave
topic: how three woven cloths differ in their structure, and what a fourth would have to do
why_this_fixture: The control. It shares no noun, no cue and no capability request pattern with the rehearsal
fixture, and it runs the identical production path: the same ledger, the same three passes, the
It carries the same SIX distinctions the rehearsal fixture is required to carry — a user
hypothesis, a visual quality, a relation or effect, a cross-image comparison, a possible
observation and a semantic remainder — because a control that exercised fewer of them would
prove the pipeline generalises only over the easy half.
prompt: the weft does different work in each of these three. in the first the warp is buried and you only read the weft, it looks almost solid; in the second the two alternate so evenly that the surface reads as a grid rather than as cloth--the third is somewhere between, the weft floats over three warps at a time and that is what gives it the diagonal. a fourth one in this family would have to decide how long a float it wants

theorist_payload.reading: Three woven samples photographed at similar scale; the interlacement differs in each and the difference is legible at the surface.

blocks.text: the first sample shows continuous horizontal runs with no interruption visible
the second sample alternates over and under at every intersection
the third sample carries runs that step sideways by one position each row
the first and third samples both hide part of the vertical set, the second hides none of it
the second sample reads as a printed grid at this scale while being an interlacement
stepping the runs sideways each row is a construction documented in industrial pattern books
the diagonal in the third sample may be a consequence of the step rather than of any dyeing

observables.success_when: both sets are located and the overlap is returned
observables.ambiguous_when: the two sets cannot be told apart at this resolution
observables.remains_interpretive: whether a high coverage figure is what makes a surface look solid

alternatives.label: measure the covered fraction over the whole sample
alternatives.consequence: one figure for the sample, and local variation is averaged away

alternatives.label: measure the covered fraction in several windows
alternatives.consequence: several figures, more cost, and variation across the sample becomes visible

observables.success_when: a period is returned in both directions
observables.ambiguous_when: the period is close to the sampling limit

observables.success_when: a run length and a per-row step are returned
observables.ambiguous_when: the runs cannot be followed across rows

targets: the covered fraction of each sample
observables.success_when: each sample yields a comparable fraction
observables.ambiguous_when: the samples are photographed at different scales

decisions.question: Measure the covered fraction over the whole sample, or in several windows?
decisions.why_now: one figure per sample makes the three directly comparable and hides variation within each; windows show the variation and make the comparison a distribution rather than a number
